# OpenCanvas

> A real-time collaborative canvas (rich text, databases, whiteboards, live cursors) that applications embed the way they embed Collabora Online. The host application owns users, permissions (ACL) and files; OpenCanvas does the editing, real-time merge (Yjs CRDT), presence, export and autosave back to the host. Rust server, React/Tiptap editor, SQLite by default, MySQL/MariaDB and Redis for clusters. Optional AI, run only in the OpenCanvas server and off by default: an in-editor assistant (plan, approval, edits in place as a visible collaborator, suggestions for existing text, run undo, limits, audit) and an MCP endpoint for external agents with host-issued tokens; models from the Claude Platform or an OpenAI-compatible server (OpenAI, vLLM, Ollama, llama.cpp). Canvas content is sent to the configured model server. Open source under the Apache License 2.0 (keep the NOTICE file when redistributing; bundled fonts under the SIL OFL). Status: 0.1.2, with best-effort support and no production SLA.

## Site
- [OpenCanvas: a collaborative canvas you embed](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/): OpenCanvas is a real-time collaborative canvas (docs, databases, whiteboards, live cursors) that your app embeds the way it embeds Collabora: your app keeps users, permissions and files; OpenCanvas does the editing and autosaves back. Open source under Apache 2.0.
- [Roadmap](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/roadmap.html): What OpenCanvas has built, what is in review and in progress, and the phases that follow, from the project's tracker.
- [Changelog](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/changelog.html): What changed in OpenCanvas and how each change was verified, from the project's integration log.
- [Interactive demo](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/app/#demo): the real editor with a sample canvas, no server; its assistant plays a scripted run, no AI server

## Documentation
- [Documentation](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/index.html): OpenCanvas documentation: run it, integrate it with your app over JWT or WOPI, the protocol, operations, security and the architecture.
- [Getting started](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/getting-started.html): Run the OpenCanvas server, the editor and the sample host on your machine, try the demo without a backend, embed it, and run the tests.
- [Release notes 0.1.2](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/release-012.html): OpenCanvas 0.1.2 release and upgrade notes for host integrations, diagramming, version history, and the headless API.
- [Release notes 0.1.0](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/release.html): OpenCanvas 0.1.0: what is included, what changed since 0.1.0-alpha.1 with its tests, upgrade notes (WOPI proof keys, MCP public URL and file scope, schema validation), known limitations and the verification checklist.
- [FAQ](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/faq.html): Answers about OpenCanvas: its status, what the Apache 2.0 licence allows, what data it keeps, how users sign in, WOPI, exports and scaling.
- [Integration guide](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/integration.html): The host contract: register your host, sign a JWT launch token, embed the editor, implement load and save callbacks, the postMessage API and the server-to-server REST API.
- [WOPI mode](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/wopi.html): Open OpenCanvas from an existing WOPI host such as Nextcloud: discovery, the WOPISrc allow-list, CheckFileInfo, GetFile, PutFile and PUT_RELATIVE.
- [Jitsi Meet](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/jitsi.html): Add a shared canvas to Jitsi Meet with one Prosody plugin and config, no Docker changes: temporary canvases, deleted when the meeting ends, blank or from a template.
- [Nextcloud](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/nextcloud.html): Create and edit .ocanvas files in Nextcloud with the opencanvas app: Nextcloud keeps files, shares and versions as a WOPI host; read-only shares open view-only and share changes reach open canvases at once.
- [Element / Matrix](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/matrix.html): Add a shared canvas to Matrix rooms as an Element widget: identity checked with the user's homeserver (OpenID), room members only, roles from power levels, temporary canvases.
- [Mattermost](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/mattermost.html): Create canvases and meeting notes in Mattermost channels, opened in the right-hand panel; the plugin is the host, files stay in Mattermost, access follows channel membership.
- [Protocol and build contract](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/protocol.html): The exact interfaces between the OpenCanvas server, the editor and the host: routes, the WebSocket protocol, the Yjs layout, the session ticket and the save outbox.
- [Operations and deployment](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/operations.html): Run OpenCanvas: the Docker image, a single node on SQLite, a cluster on MySQL or MariaDB with Redis, Helm, PDF export with Gotenberg, fonts, health and metrics.
- [Security and limits](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/security.html): OpenCanvas trust boundaries, threats and controls, default limits and what personal data it holds.
- [Capacity and sizing](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/capacity.html): Measured capacity of an OpenCanvas server: users per room and per node, memory per user and per room, and a sizing table for self-hosters.
- [AI and MCP](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/ai.html): The OpenCanvas assistant and MCP endpoint: how they work, what they may do, what is sent to the model server, the threat model and limits, and how an operator configures Claude Platform or a self-hosted model.
- [Architecture](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/architecture.html): How OpenCanvas is built: components, the launch and save flows, persistence, scaling with room owners, and the deployment shape.
- [Collaboration and presence](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/collaboration.html): How edits merge, how cursors and presence work, undo, connectivity and comments in OpenCanvas.
- [Product requirements](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/product.html): What OpenCanvas is for, for whom, what is in scope, and its non-functional targets.
- [Glossary](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/docs/glossary.html): Terms used across the OpenCanvas documentation.

## API reference
- [OpenAPI 3.1 document](https://github.com/CasualOffice/opencanvas/blob/main/crates/oc-server/api/openapi.json): the source of the reference below; a running server serves it at /api/v1/openapi.json
- [Authentication](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/authentication.html): Authenticate to the OpenCanvas API with the host key or a user token your application mints: claims, issuer and audience, scopes, roles, expiry, and full minting examples.
- [API changelog](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/changelog.html): What changed in the OpenCanvas API, release by release, from the project's CHANGELOG.md.
- [Errors](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/errors.html): OpenCanvas API errors: the RFC 9457 problem details shape, how to handle each status, and every machine code with its status and meaning.
- [Idempotency](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/idempotency.html): Retry OpenCanvas API writes safely with the Idempotency-Key header: what is stored, replays, key reuse, requests still running, and the 24-hour window.
- [API overview](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/index.html): The OpenCanvas headless API: read and change canvases from programs. Base URL, versioning, the api_v1 switch, request conventions and a first call in curl, TypeScript, Rust and Python.
- [Pagination](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/pagination.html): Page through OpenCanvas blocks and database rows with opaque, signed cursors that survive concurrent edits: limits, next_cursor, the Link header, expiry and errors.
- [Rate limits](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/rate-limits.html): OpenCanvas API rate limits: token buckets per caller and per file, the RateLimit-Policy and RateLimit headers, 429 with Retry-After, and per-host settings.
- [Admin API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/admin.html): OpenCanvas API reference, Admin: Save now (200 saved, 202 queued in the outbox, 409 conflict); Change a user's role live (none disconnects them); Final save, disconnect everyone, drop every ticket; The member list changed; drop cached answers.
- [Blocks API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/blocks.html): OpenCanvas API reference, Blocks: List top-level blocks; Read one block (also nested ones); Find blocks whose text contains q (case-insensitive); Change blocks in one atomic transaction.
- [Boards API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/boards.html): OpenCanvas API reference, Boards: Read a board's shapes; Add shapes to a board.
- [Canvas API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/canvas.html): OpenCanvas API reference, Canvas: Read a canvas as JSON blocks, Markdown or an outline.
- [Comments API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/comments.html): OpenCanvas API reference, Comments: List comment threads; Start a thread on a block or reply to one.
- [Databases API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/databases.html): OpenCanvas API reference, Databases: List databases with fields, row counts and views; Create a database block; Describe one database; Query rows; Create or update rows (at most 200); Add a field.
- [Export and import API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/files.html): OpenCanvas API reference, Export and import: Export the canvas; Import Markdown, HTML or CSV into the canvas; Stateless conversion.
- [0.1 routes (deprecated) API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/legacy.html): OpenCanvas API reference, 0.1 routes (deprecated): Patch blocks (0.1); Save now (0.1); Change a role (0.1); Close the session (0.1); Members changed (0.1); Import (0.1); Convert (0.1).
- [Members API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/members.html): OpenCanvas API reference, Members: People with access (id, name, detail; never e-mail).
- [OpenAPI document API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/meta.html): OpenCanvas API reference, OpenAPI document: This document.
- [Events and sync API](https://canvas.casualoffice.org/api/reference/streams.html): OpenCanvas API reference, Events and sync: Change events of one file, as Server-Sent Events or (with a WebSocket upgrade) JSON text messages; A ticket for the room WebSocket, so a Yjs-native client syncs the CRDT directly.
